title: Disk & storage
summary: Disk errors, retried reads and writes, file system problems and low space.

events.title: Windows found a bad block on a disk
events.meaning: The disk driver reported a bad block while reading or writing a disk.
events.causes: A failing disk, a loose or bad cable, or a bad sector.
events.next: Back up your data now, then check the disk health with the maker's tool or SMART data.

events.title: The disk driver reported a controller error
events.meaning: The driver got an error from the disk controller while talking to a disk.
events.causes: A bad cable or connection, a failing disk or controller, or a driver problem.
events.next: Check the cables and connections, update the storage drivers, and check disk health.

events.title: A disk error happened while paging memory
events.meaning: Windows had an error while moving memory data to or from a disk.
events.causes: A failing disk, a bad cable, or a USB or external drive that was disconnected.
events.next: Check disk health and connections. If it is an external drive, try another cable or port.

events.title: A disk read or write had to be retried
events.meaning: Windows asked a disk to repeat an operation because the first try failed or took too long.
events.causes: An early sign of a failing disk, a weak cable or connection, or a busy storage controller.
events.next: Check disk health and cables. If it repeats, back up your data.

events.title: The file system found damage on a volume
events.meaning: NTFS found corruption in the structure of a volume.
events.causes: An unclean shutdown, a failing disk or a bad cable.
events.next: Back up your data, then run a disk check on the volume and check the disk health.

events.title: NTFS checked a volume and found it healthy
events.meaning: Windows ran an online check of a volume and logged that it is healthy.
events.next: No action needed. A volume that is not healthy is reported by other events such as 55.

events.title: NTFS could not save data to its transaction log
events.meaning: The file system could not flush data to its transaction log, so data on the volume may be damaged.
events.causes: A failing disk, a lost connection to the drive, or a power problem.
events.next: Check the disk and its connection, then run a disk check on the volume.

events.title: The SATA storage controller did not respond in time
events.meaning: Windows had to reset a storage device because the controller did not answer in time.
events.causes: A failing disk, a poor cable or connection, or a driver problem.
events.next: Check the disk health and cables, and update the storage driver and firmware.

events.title: The NVMe storage controller did not respond in time
events.meaning: Windows had to reset an NVMe drive because it did not answer in time.
events.causes: A failing drive, a firmware or driver bug, or overheating.
events.next: Update the drive firmware and the NVMe driver, and check the drive health and temperature.

events.title: The SAS storage controller did not respond in time
events.meaning: Windows had to reset a storage device because the SAS controller did not answer in time.
events.causes: A failing disk, a bad cable or backplane, or a driver or firmware problem.
events.next: Check the disk and cable health, and update the controller driver and firmware.

events.title: A disk is almost full
events.meaning: A volume is at or close to its capacity, so Windows warns that you may need to free space.
events.causes: Large files, downloads, caches or backups filling the disk.
events.next: Free up space on the drive named in the message, or move files to another drive.
